extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of classical political philosophy (Plato)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from Plato's Republic Book V discussing the organisation and laws for the guardian class: education, gender roles, breeding, family arrangements, and the aims of legislation in the ideal State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal education for guardian women and men
rubrics_metrics.description: Women must be taught music and gymnastic and also the art of war, and practise them like the men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If women are to have the same duties as men, they must receive the same nurture and education. Ridicule at the sight of women exercising or wearing armour is misplaced if the practice serves the good of the State; experience and reason should decide, not current opinion or ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign tasks according to relevant nature (not trivial differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different natures should have different pursuits only where differences affect the pursuit; trivial differences (e.g., bald vs. hairy) are irrelevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing the State, distinguish those differences that change fitness for a role from superficial differences. Only qualities that affect capacity for an art/pursuit justify different assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select guardians by virtue and capacity, not by sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Men and women alike possess the qualities which make a guardian; selection should be of those individuals (male or female) who have the guardian temper and capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose companions/colleagues who resemble one another in capacity and character; the same natures should have the same pursuits. Natural differences in strength affect distribution of lighter/heavier labours but not eligibility for guardianship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must both obey and be able to command
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be willingness to obey in some and the power of command in others; guardians themselves must obey the laws and imitate the spirit of the laws in entrusted details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-ordered ruling class requires internal discipline: rulers must be examples of lawfulness and should embody the values they legislate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership of wives and children among guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: The wives of the guardians are to be common, their children common, and no parent is to know his own child, nor any child his parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a law of the ideal State to promote unity and remove private family loyalties that conflict with civic unity. The text separates utility (the benefit) from possibility (practical implementation) and argues for the moral/political benefits first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal living and common meals for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must live in common houses, meet at common meals, and have nothing specially his or her own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared living fosters unity and mutual regard; private possessions and household separations are presented as sources of discord and divided loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-directed breeding: pair best-with-best
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers should take care to breed from the best only; the best of either sex should be united with the best as often as possible, and inferior with inferior as seldom as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breeding should be arranged to maintain the 'breed' of guardians. This involves careful selection analogous to animal breeding, applied to humans for political ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regulated festivals and lots to organize marriages
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint festivals at which brides and bridegrooms are brought together; number of weddings to be left to rulers' discretion; devise lots so the less worthy blame luck rather than rulers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly staged, regulated mating events conceal rulers' manipulations and preserve social calm while implementing breeding policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers may employ necessary falsehoods for civic good (‘medicinal lies’)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers will find a considerable dose of falsehood and deceit necessary for the good of their subjects; these are likened to medicines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some untruths are presented as legitimate tools of statesmanship to maintain social order and to effect beneficial outcomes that would be unattainable by transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age windows for sanctioned reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Women in prime reproductive years defined as about 20–40; men from about 25–55; anyone outside this range who participates in hymeneals is committing an unholy act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction is regulated temporally to maximize physical and intellectual vigour in offspring and to align births with civic aims. Concealed births outside sanctioned periods are treated as illegitimate to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict secrecy and anonymity about parentage
rubrics_metrics.description: No parent is to know his own child; children are reared in communal folds by appointed nurses so that parentage is concealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity prevents private family loyalties from undermining civic unity. The State assigns surrogate relations and forbids recognition to reinforce communal bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose or remove inferior or deformed offspring
rubrics_metrics.description: Offspring of the inferior, or the better when deformed, are to be put away in some mysterious, unknown place (i.e., removed), while offspring of good parents are reared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective removal is prescribed to preserve the quality of the guardian class; officers are responsible for separating and disposing of undesirable offspring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nursing and childcare handled by state-appointed attendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper officers will deposit offspring with certain nurses who dwell in a separate quarter; mothers will bring infants when full of milk and will not recognize their own child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional, centralized childcare removes burdens from mothers and standardizes upbringing, aiding the State’s control over socialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and prohibitions on incestuous unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain marriages (e.g., a man may not marry his daughter or daughter's daughter, etc.) are prohibited; those considered brothers and sisters (by dating from hymeneal) are normally forbidden to intermarry, with exceptional oracle-sanctioned allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social categories constructed by the State (who is ‘brother’/‘sister’) are used to regulate permissible unions; exceptions may be granted by religious/oracular sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust breeding to demographic contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers must consider effects of wars, diseases, and similar agencies to prevent the State from becoming too large or too small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breeding policy is dynamic: rulers must modulate mating numbers and pairings to maintain population stability and the desired distribution of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor and reward courageous guardians to encourage procreation
rubrics_metrics.description: Braver and better youth might have greater facilities of intercourse given them as honours and rewards; bravery justifies rewards that encourage more offspring from the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social incentives are built into the polity to channel reproductive advantage toward those who serve the State's ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign lighter labours to women according to relative physical strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Women share the same duties as men generally, but in the distribution of labours the lighter are to be assigned to the women, who are the weaker natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges physical differences while maintaining equality of duties and access to education/roles; does not exclude women from military or civic tasks except to allocate heavier tasks where strength matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education (music and gymnastic) as means to make the best citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: The same education which makes a man a good guardian will make a woman a good guardian; the arts of music and gymnastic present in the described manner produce the best men and women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural and physical education shapes moral character and civic competence; the regime of education is central to producing the ideal guardian class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of feeling as the chief aim of legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest good is unity; the greatest evil is discord and plurality where unity ought to reign. Unity arises where citizens share pleasures and pains and apply 'mine' and 'not mine' in the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws and social arrangements should prioritize bonds that align individual affections with the common good; family privatism is a chief source of disunity to be neutralized by communal institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize kinship in practice, not only in name
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians are to regard one another as brothers/sisters/parents/children in both name and action; the language of kinship must be backed by mutual care and obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels of kinship must correspond to real behaviours and duties. If the State calls citizens 'father'/'mother' it must ensure the social practices that make those terms meaningful (reciprocal care, reverence, duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent private feeling by aligning language and practice of family ties
rubrics_metrics.description: The State should make family-language pervasive and lived so that expressions of kinship are not mere lip-service but actual social bonds, reinforcing concord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rituals, laws, and public life should cultivate common feelings so that private attachments do not disrupt civic unity; the civic naming-and-nurture system replaces biological family loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: State control of procreative legitimacy and punishment of unsanctioned births
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts of intercourse outside sanctioned hymeneals or outside prescribed ages render offspring 'bastards to the State' and are to be dealt with (prevented from being maintained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State criminalizes and manages illegitimate conceptions to preserve social and moral order; parents engaging in unsanctioned unions must understand consequences for offspring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of engineered social narratives to deflect blame
rubrics_metrics.description: When lotteries or public devices are used to match partners, the less worthy will blame luck rather than the rulers for undesirable matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulating apparent randomness preserves social peace and masks the rulers' selection, reducing resentment and resistance among the populace.
